笙簧是傳統韓國氣鳴樂器，屬自由簧口風琴，源自中國笙，並與日本笙相關。其構造為十七: The saenghwang is a traditional Korean aerophone, a free-reed mouth organ derived from the Chinese sheng and related to the Japanese shō. It is built from seventeen bamboo pipes set vertically into a wind chest, each pipe holding a metal free reed; the wind chest was traditionally made of a dried gourd and is now more often metal or wood. It can sound several notes at once, usually three together, two of them an octave apart and the third a fourth or a fifth below. It is used mainly in chamber music, often with the danso and the yanggeum; in old Korean paintings gisaeng are often shown playing it.
笙簧為朝鮮半島傳統氣鳴樂器，屬自由簧口風琴，源自中國笙，與日本笙同由笙衍生。它在: The saenghwang is a traditional free-reed aerophone of the Korean peninsula, derived from the Chinese sheng, as is the Japanese shō. It is recorded as early as the Three Kingdoms period of Korea, where it was historically called saeng; the name also appears in the Goryeo period. The Chinese sheng continued to arrive, and the Goryeo court received one as a gift from the Song court in 1116. In 1406 the Yongle Emperor of the Ming presented a sheng to the Korean court. It was already being made in Korea in the reign of Sejong. Making was interrupted for a time during the Japanese invasions of Korea from 1592 to 1598; afterwards it continued into the Japanese colonial period, and after the founding of Korea its players entered the National Gugak Center, with the government also supporting some of them.
笙簧為朝鮮半島傳統自由簧氣鳴樂器，發聲體由十七根竹管構成，每管裝金屬自由簧片，垂: The saenghwang is a traditional free-reed aerophone of the Korean peninsula. Its sounding body consists of seventeen bamboo pipes, each holding a metal free reed, set vertically into a wind chest. The wind chest was traditionally made of dried gourd, and metal or wood is more common today. The source does not state the materials of the other parts, so no guess is made.
笙簧音色溫潤悠遠，具有典雅的東方韻味。其音質介於明亮與暗沉之間，帶有柔和的穿透感: The saenghwang has a warm, distant timbre with an elegant Eastern character. Its sound lies between bright and dark, with a soft carrying quality and no lack of dignity. Its range is wide, spanning several octaves, with a deep, full low register and a clear, sweet high one. Its resonance is distinctive: the bamboo pipes and the metal reeds together produce rich layers of overtones, which gives its sound a strong national colour. Compared with the sharpness of Western reed instruments, the saenghwang is quieter and more inward; compared with the Chinese sheng of the same East Asian region, it has more of a secluded elegance. In ensemble with the danso and the yanggeum it usually provides harmonic support, and its warm tone forms a harmonious layer with the other instruments, creating a musical atmosphere of long-standing antiquity.
